note: Narrow, deliberate correction: VW group's Pumpe-Duese (unit-injector) TDIs were all given 'VW 501.01/505.00', which is not a valid approval for them. In a PD engine a profiled camshaft lobe drives the injector plunger directly at over 2050 bar — the highest loading of any TDI fuel system — and VW created 505.01 specifically for the anti-wear package that contact needs. A 505.00 oil accelerates cam-lobe wear, the classic and expensive PD failure. 507.00 does not substitute for 505.01 either; it is the separate requirement for the particulate-filter versions. The rest of the VW catalogue (common-rail TDIs on 504.00/507.00, petrols on 502.00/505.01) already carries plausible approvals and is left alone. Codes are split 1.9 vs 2.0 for sump capacity, and DPF vs non-DPF for the approval.

engines.source: 1.9 TDI PD fitted with a particulate filter (Golf V, Passat B6, Caddy, Octavia II). The DPF makes the low-SAPS 507.00 oil a requirement in place of 505.01.

1.9 TDI PD without a particulate filter (Golf IV/V, Bora, Polo, Passat B5.5, Leon, Octavia I/II, A3 8L/8P). RWC Motorsport TDI fuel-system guide and TDIClub: the unit injector is driven by a dedicated camshaft lobe at pressures above 2050 bar and requires an oil certified to VW 505.01 — 505.00 is explicitly insufficient and 507.00 does not replace it.
2.0 TDI PD fitted with a particulate filter (Passat B6, Golf V, Touran, Octavia II, A3 8P). 507.00 in place of 505.01 because of the DPF.
2.0 TDI PD without a particulate filter (Golf V, Touran, Passat B6, Octavia II, A3 8P). Same 505.01 unit-injector requirement as the 1.9; the 2.0 takes a slightly smaller fill.
